newsitem.title: USA: Paxon says not involved in any Gingrich challenge.
newsitem.headline: Paxon says not involved in any Gingrich challenge.

text.p: New York Republican Representative Bill Paxon, who quit a key party post last week after an internal power struggle, denied on Sunday that he participated in a plan to oust House Speaker Newt Gingrich.
Paxon, a rising conservative star who resigned his post as chairman of the Republican leadership on Thursday, also said he had no desire to replace Gingrich as speaker.
"At no time have I ever been involved in efforts to overthrow the speaker that I worked so hard to elect," Paxon said on NBC's Meet the Press television programme.

"Last week, I tried to work to defuse a problem that you have well noted. Mistakes were made ... I accept responsibility, personal responsibility, for the way I handled this matter and I resigned," Paxon said.
Gingrich has been plagued by internal party problems since he narrowly won re-election as speaker in January. He was reprimanded and fined by his colleagues for ethics violations.
In his resignation, the 43-year-old Paxon, cited "a growing crisis of confidence" within the party and the need to "mend its wounds."
Paxon told NBC he resigned after it became apparent that Gingrich had lost confidence in him.

"When I looked in the speaker's eye, it was clear he had lost confidence in me," Paxon said. "You take responsibility for your mistakes and that is what I did. That does not in any way indicate, and it for sure isn't, that I was involved in any efforts to overthrow the speaker.
When asked if he would be interested in becoming speaker if and when Gingrich moves on, Paxon replied: "No. Period. I never have been interested and don't intend to be."

Paxon headed the National Republican Congressional Committee and helped engineer the party's recapture of the House in the 1994 elections after 40 years in the minority. He is married to Representative Susan Molinari, Republican of New York, who will resign in August to become a CBS weekend television news anchor.
